scenarios.name: abandoned-query-does-not-block-pool
scenarios.description: A client that drops its connection mid-query must not block the next client until the query ends.

scenarios.name: aborted-transaction-not-reused
scenarios.description: A client that disconnects inside an aborted transaction must not pass it to the next client.
steps: [a] simple: SET LOCAL statement_timeout = 100; SELECT pg_sleep(1); COMMIT

scenarios.name: advisory-lock-released-on-disconnect
scenarios.description: A session advisory lock must be released when the client that took it disconnects.
steps: [check (direct)] simple: DO $$ BEGIN FOR i IN 1..60 LOOP EXIT WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_locks WHERE locktype = 'advisory' AND objid = 424242); PERFORM pg_sleep(0.05); END LOOP; END $$
[check (direct)] simple: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_locks WHERE locktype = 'advisory' AND objid = 424242

scenarios.name: advisory-lock-survives-own-transactions
scenarios.description: A session advisory lock must stay held by the client that took it, across its later transactions.
steps: [a] simple: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_locks WHERE locktype = 'advisory' AND objid = 424243 AND pid = pg_backend_pid()
[a] simple: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_locks WHERE locktype = 'advisory' AND objid = 424243 AND pid = pg_backend_pid()

scenarios.name: cancel-from-idle-client-is-harmless
scenarios.description: A CancelRequest from a client with no running query must not cancel another client's query.

scenarios.name: cancel-reaches-running-query
scenarios.description: A CancelRequest must cancel the client's running query.

scenarios.name: cancel-under-saturated-pool
scenarios.description: A CancelRequest must still cancel the query when other clients are queued for a server connection.

scenarios.name: copy-from-stdin
scenarios.description: COPY FROM STDIN through the pooler must load every row.
steps: [a] send: query COPY pp_copy FROM STDIN

scenarios.name: copy-to-stdout
scenarios.description: COPY TO STDOUT through the pooler must return every row unchanged, over the simple and the extended protocol.
steps: [a] send: query COPY (SELECT * FROM (VALUES (1, 'a'), (2, NULL), (3, E'tab\there')) v (x, t) ORDER BY x) TO STDOUT
[a] send: parse - COPY (SELECT g FROM generate_series(1, 3) g) TO STDOUT / bind - - / execute - / sync

scenarios.name: cursor-isolated-between-clients
scenarios.description: A WITH HOLD cursor declared by one client must not be visible to another client.
steps: [a] simple: DECLARE pp_cur CURSOR WITH HOLD FOR SELECT generate_series(1, 3)::text

scenarios.name: cursor-survives-own-transactions
scenarios.description: A WITH HOLD cursor must stay usable by the client that declared it, across its later transactions.
steps: [a] simple: DECLARE pp_own_cur CURSOR WITH HOLD FOR SELECT generate_series(1, 3)::text

scenarios.name: deallocate-all-isolated
scenarios.description: DEALLOCATE ALL from one client must not remove another client's prepared statements.

scenarios.name: discard-all-in-transaction-fails
scenarios.description: DISCARD ALL inside a transaction block must fail with 25001, not be answered by the pooler.

scenarios.name: discard-all-resets-settings
scenarios.description: DISCARD ALL must reset the client's settings to their defaults.

scenarios.name: empty-search-path-from-set-config
scenarios.description: An empty search_path set with set_config() must survive another client changing it.

scenarios.name: listen-notify-delivered
scenarios.description: A client that ran LISTEN must receive NOTIFY messages sent by another client.

scenarios.name: load-isolated-between-clients
scenarios.description: A library one client loads with LOAD must not show up for another client.

scenarios.name: multi-statement-begin-error
scenarios.description: An error in BEGIN; ...; COMMIT must return the error and leave the transaction aborted, as Postgres does. Otherwise the app's next statements run outside any transaction.
steps: [app] simple: BEGIN; INSERT INTO pp_multi_missing VALUES (1); COMMIT
[app] simple: BEGIN; INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (1); SELECT 1/0; COMMIT
[app] simple: BEGIN READ ONLY; INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (2); COMMIT
[check (direct)] simple: SELECT coalesce(array_agg(x ORDER BY x)::text, '{}') FROM pp_multi

scenarios.name: multi-statement-begin-left-open
scenarios.description: BEGIN; ... without COMMIT in the same string must leave the transaction open on the client's server connection. Otherwise its statements are lost or run outside the transaction.
steps: [app] simple: BEGIN; INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (1)
[check (direct)] simple: SELECT coalesce(array_agg(x ORDER BY x)::text, '{}') FROM pp_multi
[other] background: SELECT pg_current_xact_id_if_assigned() IS NULL AS own_transaction
[check (direct)] simple: SELECT coalesce(array_agg(x ORDER BY x)::text, '{}') FROM pp_multi

scenarios.name: multi-statement-begin-not-first
scenarios.description: A simple query with BEGIN after its first statement must run every statement, and a transaction it leaves open must stay open.
steps: [app] simple: SELECT 1; BEGIN; INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (1); COMMIT
[app] simple: SELECT count(*) FROM pp_multi; START TRANSACTION; INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (2); COMMIT
[app] simple: SELECT 1; BEGIN; INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (3)
[check (direct)] simple: SELECT coalesce(array_agg(x ORDER BY x)::text, '{}') FROM pp_multi
[other] background: SELECT pg_current_xact_id_if_assigned() IS NULL AS own_transaction
[check (direct)] simple: SELECT coalesce(array_agg(x ORDER BY x)::text, '{}') FROM pp_multi

scenarios.name: multi-statement-begin-variants
scenarios.description: Every way to write BEGIN or START TRANSACTION at the start of a simple query must run every statement, with its options. Otherwise statements silently don't run, or run at the wrong isolation level.
steps: [app] simple: begin; insert into pp_multi values (1); commit
[app] simple:    BEGIN ;  INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (2) ; COMMIT ;
[app] simple: /* leading */ BEGIN; INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (3); COMMIT

[app] simple: -- leading
BEGIN; INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (4); COMMIT
[app] simple: BEGIN WORK; INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (5); COMMIT WORK
[app] simple: BEGIN TRANSACTION; INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (6); END
[app] simple: START TRANSACTION; INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (7); COMMIT
[app] simple: BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ; SELECT current_setting('transaction_isolation'); COMMIT
[app] simple: START TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE, READ ONLY; SELECT current_setting('transaction_isolation'), current_setting('transaction_read_only'); COMMIT
[app] simple: BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ
[check (direct)] simple: SELECT coalesce(array_agg(x ORDER BY x)::text, '{}') FROM pp_multi

scenarios.name: multi-statement-begin
scenarios.description: A simple query that starts with BEGIN must run every statement in the string.
steps: [app] simple: BEGIN; INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (1); COMMIT

scenarios.name: multi-statement-commit-first
scenarios.description: A simple query that starts with COMMIT, ROLLBACK or END must run the statements after it. Otherwise the app's later statements in the string silently don't run.
steps: [app] simple: COMMIT; INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (2)
[app] simple: ROLLBACK; INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (4)
[app] simple: COMMIT; INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (5)
[app] simple: ROLLBACK; INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (6)
[app] simple: END; INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (7)
[check (direct)] simple: SELECT coalesce(array_agg(x ORDER BY x)::text, '{}') FROM pp_multi

scenarios.name: multi-statement-error-aborts-transaction
scenarios.description: A simple query that opens a transaction and fails inside it must leave that transaction aborted. Otherwise the app's next statements are committed one by one instead of rejected.
steps: [app] simple: SELECT 1; BEGIN; INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (1); INSERT INTO pp_multi_missing VALUES (1); COMMIT
[check (direct)] simple: SELECT coalesce(array_agg(x ORDER BY x)::text, '{}') FROM pp_multi

scenarios.name: parameter-status-after-set
scenarios.description: After a SET of a parameter Postgres reports, the client must get a ParameterStatus with the new value.

scenarios.name: prepare-in-aborted-transaction
scenarios.description: Parse inside a failed transaction must return 25P02, not succeed from a cache.

scenarios.name: prepared-statement-survives-other-clients
scenarios.description: A protocol-level prepared statement must still work after other clients used the pool.

scenarios.name: protocol-error-after-flush
scenarios.description: An error in a request that ends with Flush instead of Sync must be sent right away, and Sync must recover.
steps: [a] send: parse - SELECT 'recovered'::text / bind - - / execute - / sync

scenarios.name: protocol-four-pipelined-requests
scenarios.description: Four requests pipelined on one connection, each ending in Sync, must all get their results.
steps: [a] send: parse - SELECT 1 / bind - - / execute - / sync / parse - SELECT 2 / bind - - / execute - / sync / parse - SELECT 3 / bind - - / execute - / sync / parse - SELECT 4 / bind - - / execute - / sync

scenarios.name: protocol-multi-statement-transaction
scenarios.description: Transaction control over the extended protocol must behave as on Postgres: a multi-statement Parse fails, and BEGIN and COMMIT in a pipeline or in their own Sync run on the server.
steps: [app] send: parse - BEGIN; INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (1); COMMIT / sync
[app] send: parse - BEGIN / bind - - / execute - / parse - INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (2) / bind - - / execute - / parse - COMMIT / bind - - / execute - / sync
[app] send: parse - BEGIN / bind - - / execute - / sync
[app] send: parse - INSERT INTO pp_multi VALUES (3) / bind - - / execute - / sync
[check (direct)] simple: SELECT coalesce(array_agg(x ORDER BY x)::text, '{}') FROM pp_multi
[other] background: SELECT pg_current_xact_id_if_assigned() IS NULL AS own_transaction
[app] send: parse - COMMIT / bind - - / execute - / sync
[check (direct)] simple: SELECT coalesce(array_agg(x ORDER BY x)::text, '{}') FROM pp_multi

scenarios.name: protocol-pipeline-recovers-after-error
scenarios.description: In a pipeline, a failing request must not affect the request after the next Sync.
steps: [a] send: parse - SELECT 1/0 / bind - - / execute - / sync / parse - SELECT 'second'::text / bind - - / execute - / sync

scenarios.name: protocol-pipelined-statements
scenarios.description: Several named statements prepared and run in one pipeline must all return their own results.
steps: [a] send: parse p1 SELECT 'one'::text / parse p2 SELECT 'two'::text / bind - p2 / execute - / bind - p1 / execute - / sync

scenarios.name: protocol-prepare-survives-server-change
scenarios.description: A protocol-level prepared statement must stay usable by its client while another client holds the server connection it was prepared on.
steps: [a] simple: INSERT INTO pp_hog_pid VALUES ('a', pg_backend_pid()) ON CONFLICT (who) DO UPDATE SET pid = excluded.pid
[c] precondition simple: SELECT pg_backend_pid() = (SELECT pid FROM pp_hog_pid WHERE who = 'a')

scenarios.name: protocol-statement-names-isolated
scenarios.description: Two clients can prepare protocol-level statements with the same name, and each runs its own.
steps: [a] send: parse s1 SELECT 'from a'::text / sync
[b] send: parse s1 SELECT 'from b'::text / sync

scenarios.name: protocol-statement-reparsed-after-close
scenarios.description: After Close, a statement name can be prepared again with different SQL, and the new SQL runs.

scenarios.name: protocol-unnamed-statement-survives-other-clients
scenarios.description: The unnamed statement stays usable until the same client replaces it, even if other clients ran queries.

scenarios.name: search-path-isolated-between-clients
scenarios.description: A client's empty search_path must still be empty after another client changed it.

scenarios.name: set-does-not-leak-after-disconnect
scenarios.description: Settings from a client that disconnected must not show up for the next client.

scenarios.name: set-isolated-between-clients
scenarios.description: A plain SET from one client must not change the setting another client sees.

scenarios.name: set-local-default-after-set-local
scenarios.description: SET LOCAL ... TO DEFAULT after an earlier SET LOCAL in the same transaction, then COMMIT, must leave the session value.
steps: [a] simple: SET LOCAL statement_timeout TO DEFAULT

scenarios.name: set-local-reverts-after-commit
scenarios.description: SET LOCAL ... TO DEFAULT must not change the session value, outside or inside a transaction.
steps: [a] simple: SET LOCAL statement_timeout TO DEFAULT
[a] simple: SET LOCAL statement_timeout TO DEFAULT

scenarios.name: set-role-isolated-between-clients
scenarios.description: SET ROLE from one client must not change the role another client runs as.

scenarios.name: set-role-reset-after-pinned-disconnect
scenarios.description: A client that held an advisory lock and ran SET ROLE must not pass its role to the next client.

scenarios.name: set-survives-server-change
scenarios.description: A session setting must stay in effect for its client while another client holds the server connection it was set on.
steps: [a] simple: INSERT INTO pp_hog_pid VALUES ('a', pg_backend_pid()) ON CONFLICT (who) DO UPDATE SET pid = excluded.pid
[c] precondition simple: SELECT pg_backend_pid() = (SELECT pid FROM pp_hog_pid WHERE who = 'a')

scenarios.name: sql-prepare-isolated-between-clients
scenarios.description: A statement made with SQL PREPARE must be usable by the client that made it, and only by it.
steps: [a] simple: PREPARE pp_q AS SELECT 'from a'::text

scenarios.name: sql-prepare-survives-server-change
scenarios.description: A statement prepared with SQL PREPARE must stay usable by its client while another client holds the server connection it was prepared on.
steps: [a] simple: PREPARE pp_hog_stmt AS SELECT 'from a'::text
[a] simple: INSERT INTO pp_hog_pid VALUES ('a', pg_backend_pid()) ON CONFLICT (who) DO UPDATE SET pid = excluded.pid
[c] precondition simple: SELECT pg_backend_pid() = (SELECT pid FROM pp_hog_pid WHERE who = 'a')

scenarios.name: temp-table-isolated-between-clients
scenarios.description: A temp table created by one client must not be visible to another client.
steps: [a] simple: CREATE TEMP TABLE pp_tmp (x int)

scenarios.name: temp-table-survives-own-transactions
scenarios.description: A temp table must stay usable by the client that created it, across its later transactions.
steps: [a] simple: CREATE TEMP TABLE pp_own_tmp (x int)

scenarios.name: temp-table-survives-server-change
scenarios.description: A temp table must stay usable by its client while another client holds the server connection it was created on.
steps: [a] simple: CREATE TEMP TABLE pp_hog_tmp (x int)
[a] simple: INSERT INTO pp_hog_pid VALUES ('a', pg_backend_pid()) ON CONFLICT (who) DO UPDATE SET pid = excluded.pid
[c] precondition simple: SELECT pg_backend_pid() = (SELECT pid FROM pp_hog_pid WHERE who = 'a')
[a] simple: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS pp_hog_tmp
